nodes.description: The one encouraging therapeutic result in this disease, and it is preclinical. Systemic delivery of a neurotrophic AAV-PHP.B vector carrying the Slc25a46 coding sequence to knockout mice rescued premature death, improved nerve conduction and mobility, restored respiratory-chain complex activities, and normalised mitochondrial morphology in central and peripheral nervous tissue. It is recorded here as a rescue arm rather than as a treatment, because nothing has been tried in patients.

nodes.description: SLC25A46 normally occupies discrete foci at mitochondrial branch points and tube tips together with DRP1 and OPA1, and essentially every fission or fusion event is marked by such a focus. It is a hub in three complexes at once: with the fusion GTPases MFN1, MFN2 and OPA1, with the MICOS cristae-organising complex through MIC60, and with the ER membrane protein complex at ER-mitochondria contacts. Losing it therefore disrupts dynamics, cristae and lipid handling together rather than one at a time.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of SLC25A46 causes neurodegeneration by affecting mitochondrial dynamics and energy production in mice.
evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that loss of SLC25A46 causes degeneration in neurons by affecting mitochondrial dynamics and energy production.

nodes.description: An independently derived loss-of-function mutant that reproduces ataxia, optic atrophy and cerebellar hypoplasia and is fully rescued by expressing the human orthologue, which is strong evidence that the lesion is the gene. It adds neuromuscular junction abnormalities and a lymphoid phenotype not seen before.

evidence.reference_title: Novel insights into SLC25A46-related pathologies in a genetic mouse model.
evidence.snippet: Our mutant mice provide a valid model for understanding the mechanistic basis of the complex SLC25A46-mediated pathologies, as well as for screening potential therapeutic interventions.

nodes.description: The developmental model from the founding study. Morphants have fewer retinal ganglion cell axons reaching the tectum, shorter motor axon tracts, and motor terminals showing blebbing and dying back.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SLC25A46, encoding a UGO1-like protein, cause an optic atrophy spectrum disorder.
evidence.snippet: Loss of function in cultured cells and in zebrafish unexpectedly leads to increased mitochondrial connectivity, while severely affecting the development and maintenance of neurons in the fish.
